To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quaternary structure of human COHbs C and S is R2 in the presence of a precipitant, PEG 400.
human hemoglobin crystallizes in the R2 state at neutral pH and in the presence of a small molecular weight precipitant, PEG 400.
the R2 state of human COHbc and COHbs is observed crystallography at neutral pH and physiological conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of human hemoglobin in the R2 state.
the structural characterization of human hemoglobin under conditions that may be relevant to the biological environment.
the structure of hemoglobin and the mechanism by which oxygen is transported in the blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the R2 quatermary structure is a stable and physiologically relevant state for the beta6 mutant human hemoglobins.

the betaE6K and betaE6V mutants are more prone than wild-type human hemoglobin to crystallize as R2 at neutral pH and that the R2 structure is not observed for wild-type hemoglobin under physiological conditions.
the R2 structure is not a physiological intermediate state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R2 quatemary structure is observed at neutral pH in human hemoglobin mutants that have been engineered to have higher solubilities.
the R2 state can be stabilized by a combination of mutations and/or precipitants.
the R2 quaterary state of COHbS is a stable state at neutral pH and that it can be induced by the beta6 mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the R2 quatemary state of hemoglobin is a stable, physiologically relevant state under conditions that mimic the cytosol.
the R2 state can be crystallized under physiological conditions and is a viable quaternary state.
the R2 quatemary structure of human hemoglobin can be stabilized under physiological conditions by the introduction of beta6 mutants.
